title: bank-saturation-and-throttle-field-journal
body:
Purpose:
This is a working field journal capturing a set of oddball runs from the last two weeks where the KV cache showed high eviction churn coincident with a sudden jump in service latency. Goal is to capture observations, quick hypotheses, instrumentation misses, and immediate mitigations so we can prioritize follow-ups.

Context / why this felt different:
- Several multi-tenant nodes started showing p95/p99 latency regressions on generation workloads with medium-length prompts (avg seqlen 384) starting around 2024-09-10.
- Eviction telemetry (counts/time) spiked ~3x on the affected hosts; paging events also increased but not proportionally.
- Usual suspects (batching change, rollout, model swap) were ruled out: same model version and batching config as baseline.

What we ran (short log):
- Run A (2024-09-11 09:30): synthetic sketch workload, seqlen distribution 128/256/512 (30/50/20), steady-state QPS 420, batch size cap 8. Observed slow climb in eviction rate starting ~15m in.
- Run B (2024-09-12 13:20): replay of production traces on same machines with request skew introduced (hotkeys pinned to 2 tenants). Eviction rate doubled within 5m; overall memory bandwidth utilization on device rose from ~62% -> ~88%.
- Run C (2024-09-14 16:05): instrumented run with per-bank counters exported (via allocator hook), and KV residency sampling (1/500 requests). Showed a concentrated working set across 2 banks with repeated churn.

Key telemetry snippets (extracted):
- Eviction rate: baseline ~2.4 evictions/sec -> spike ~7.9 evictions/sec during incidents.
- Paging events (IO stalls): baseline ~0.02/sec -> incident ~0.08/sec (smaller relative increase).
- Device mem BW estimated (from perf counters): 680 GB/s -> 920 GB/s at spike.
- Latency impact: p50 steady, p95 up 25–40ms, p99 up by 80–140ms depending on load.
- Reuse rate (windowed per-key): global reuse fell from 0.72 -> 0.45 within affected shard.

What the per-bank sampling suggested:
- Two banks handling ~60% of active keys in the sample; other banks underutilized.
- When the hot banks hit ~92% of their local allocator quota, eviction heuristics kicked in aggressively even though global residency still had small headroom.
- Eviction policy bias: current allocator is per-bank-first (local fairness) which causes cross-bank hotspots to evict aggressively rather than reshuffle across banks.

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Bank-local saturation hysteresis: allocator treats each bank independently with a tight local cap. When a bank becomes hot, it evicts aggressively even though other banks have spare residency; eviction work increases memory bus activity -> increases BW -> slows KV warmups -> reduces reuse -> more evictions. Feedback loop.
2) Eviction thrash due to LRU granularity mismatch: our LRU aging is coarse (per-page of keys) so many cold keys co-allocate on same page as hot keys leading to repeated page-level evictions and re-reads.
3) Migration/defragmentation delay: rebalancing across banks is asynchronous and only triggers on threshold breaches; latency-to-reshuffle allows the hotspot to thrash for tens of seconds.
4) OS-level or hypervisor background housekeeping correlated (but not causal): we saw some host-level DMA bursts at times that roughly align with when device BW spikes. Might amplify but not root cause.

Instrumentation gaps we noticed:
- No fine-grained per-key access trace (sampling is very sparse) — we need a short burst tracer to capture full access sequences for 10s of seconds.
- Bank-level counters are available but not correlated into traces with eviction decision ids. Hard to link an eviction to the exact access that triggered it.
- No explicit metric for "bank imbalance" (we only export per-bank residency at 1m granularity).

Quick experiments & results:
- Experiment 1: Temporarily increased per-bank soft cap by +30% on affected hosts; eviction spikes dropped by ~45% and p99 reduced ~30ms. BUT memory pressure rose and other tenants experienced slightly elevated p50. Tradeoff shows bank-local cap is key lever.
- Experiment 2: Enabled conservative cross-bank steal: allow eviction to prefer global low-hotness banks when local bank >95% quota. Reduced eviction rate but introduced extra pointer walks (small CPU overhead). Net p99 improvement ~25%.
- Experiment 3: Synthetic page co-location test: intentionally colocated keys on same page and then hot-swapped access; observed 2x read-amplification compared to fine-grained layout. Confirms LRU granularity hypothesis.

Immediate mitigations applied (temporary, short-lived):
- Rollout: soft cap bump on nodes in the affected AZ (2024-09-16 02:00) to arrest immediate thrash.
- Telemetry: added a high-frequency per-bank residency scrape (10s) to tracing pipeline for next 48h.
- Debug mode: enabled a 20s burst tracer on three hosts for reproducer capture; artifacts pushed to /diag/kvcap/sep2024-logs.

Deeper changes to consider (priority):
- Priority A (high): Implement bank-aware eviction policy: when local bank exceeds threshold and global free residency exists, prefer cross-bank steals before local evictions. Add hysteresis to avoid oscillation.
- Priority B: Reduce LRU aging granularity — move from page-level window to sub-page key-level metadata for hotness scores. Cost: memory overhead per-key metadata + engineering risk.
- Priority C: Active rebalancer: pro-actively migrate pinned hot keys to underutilized banks when a sustained imbalance is detected. Needs fast low-overhead migration path.
- Priority D: Expose bank imbalance as an alert signal (on-call) and as a knob in Dedicated plans for tenants that need isolation guarantees.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Why did the problem surface in this cluster and not others? Potential factors: workload skew, tenancy mix, slightly older allocator runtime build on those nodes (build id 2024.07.31). Need to correlate builds.
- Are there cross-layer interactions with host kernel DMA scheduler? We saw DMA bursts but need better host-side traces.
- Does quantized model kernel behavior change access patterns (e.g., different KV touch patterns)? We should replay same traces across quantized vs fp16 containers.

Next steps (actionable owners):
- Maya C: land high-frequency per-bank scrape to prod tracing (done 2024-09-18).
- Arjun P: prototype bank-aware eviction policy in simulator, perf-run on ci-gpu-3 (ETA 1 week).
- Leah G: validate allocator binary versions across affected hosts and roll a canary with the latest allocator (ETA 3 days).
- SRE: enable short-term alert for sustained bank imbalance > 20% for 2m (TBD).

Notes to self / heuristics remembered for future runs:
- Watch mem BW as a first-order signal: sudden increases concurrent with evictions probably mean eviction-induced read-amplification rather than client QPS.
- Hot-spotting often shows as reuse-rate collapse locally before global metrics move; we should surface a "local reuse drop" metric.
- Small config changes (soft cap bump) can buy time to gather trace but are not long-term solutions.

Appendix: raw sample trace snippet (anonymized):
- t=0: baseline resident keys per bank [4.2k, 3.9k, 1.1k, 1.3k, 0.9k, 0.8k]
- t=60s: [5.1k, 4.8k, 1.2k, 1.5k, 0.9k, 0.8k] (banks 0/1 hot)
- eviction events collated: evict_id 0x7f3a (bank 0) -> re-request 120ms later -> extra BW spike

If you read this and have other angle (e.g., kernel tracing, PMU counters we didn't pull), add notes inline. We want a minimal reproducible harness (one host, synthetic skewed workload, per-bank tracer) and to avoid global rollouts until we validate the bank-aware policy in simulator.

-- Maya
